all_formulas.pitfall: Albrecht ratios not universally accepted; use with soil pH test.
all_formulas.decision: Ca < 60%: apply lime/gypsum. Mg < 10%: apply dolomite.
all_formulas.notes: Source: Albrecht (1975); USDA-NRCS.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: نسبة ألبريكت — الأهداف المثالية للكاتيونات.
all_formulas.part: Trusted-Reference Formulas (FAO-56, USDA-NRCS, ASABE, IPCC, NRC)

all_formulas.name: Soil pH Adjustment (Lime Requirement)
all_formulas.variables:
pH_target = desired pH (e.g. 6.5)
pH_current = measured pH
CEC = cation exchange capacity (meq/100g)
BD = bulk density (g/cm³)
D = depth (cm)
0.5 = empirical lime factor
all_formulas.purpose: Lime dose to raise soil pH — depends on buffering capacity.
all_formulas.example: Target 6.5, current 5.5, CEC=15, BD=1.3, D=15cm → Lime = 1×15×1.3×15×0.5 = 146 t/ha (x2 to convert to CaCO₃).
all_formulas.pitfall: Using SMP buffer incorrectly — only works on certain soils.
all_formulas.decision: Apply in 2 split doses 6 months apart; retest after 1 year.
all_formulas.notes: Source: USDA-NRCS; Shoemaker-McLean-Pratt (SMP) buffer.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: جرعة الجير لرفع درجة حموضة التربة.
all_formulas.part: Trusted-Reference Formulas (FAO-56, USDA-NRCS, ASABE, IPCC, NRC)

all_formulas.name: Water Productivity (Crop)
all_formulas.variables:
Y = crop yield (kg/ha)
ETc = actual evapotranspiration (m³/ha)
WP = water productivity (kg/m³)
all_formulas.purpose: kg of crop per m³ of water — key metric for water-scarce agriculture.
all_formulas.example: Wheat: Y=6000, ETc=5000m³ → WP=1.2 kg/m³. Global benchmark: 1.0-1.5.
all_formulas.pitfall: Using irrigation volume instead of ETc — ignores rain and soil water.
all_formulas.decision: WP < 0.8: improve variety, irrigation timing, or mulching.
all_formulas.notes: Source: FAO Water Paper; Molden (2007).
all_formulas.purpose_ar: كجم محصول لكل م³ ماء — مقياس رئيسي للزراعة المحدودة المياه.
all_formulas.part: Trusted-Reference Formulas (FAO-56, USDA-NRCS, ASABE, IPCC, NRC)

all_formulas.name: Irrigation Water Use Efficiency
all_formulas.variables:
Y_irrig = yield with irrigation
Y_rainfed = yield without irrigation
I = irrigation applied (m³/ha)
all_formulas.purpose: Marginal productivity of irrigation — justifies irrigation investment.
all_formulas.example: Y_irrig=8000, Y_rainfed=5000, I=3000 → IWUE = 1.0 kg/m³ additional yield per m³ water.
all_formulas.pitfall: Comparing IWUE across climates — arid regions show higher values.
all_formulas.decision: IWUE < 0.5: reconsider irrigation investment.
all_formulas.notes: Source: FAO; Brouwer & Prins (1989).
all_formulas.purpose_ar: الإنتاجية الحدية للري.
all_formulas.part: Trusted-Reference Formulas (FAO-56, USDA-NRCS, ASABE, IPCC, NRC)

all_formulas.name: Leaching Requirement (LR)
all_formulas.variables:
EC_iw = irrigation water salinity (dS/m)
EC_threshold = crop salt tolerance threshold (dS/m)
all_formulas.purpose: Extra water needed to flush salts below root zone.
all_formulas.example: Tomato EC_threshold=2.5, EC_iw=3.0 → LR = 3.0/(12.5-3.0) = 0.32 → apply 32% extra water.
all_formulas.pitfall: Using EC of saturation extract (ECe) for EC_iw — wrong scale.
all_formulas.decision: If LR > 0.5, switch to salt-tolerant variety or blend water.
all_formulas.notes: Source: FAO-56; Maas-Hoffman (1977) salt tolerance.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: الماء الإضافي لطرد الأملاح تحت منطقة الجذور.
all_formulas.part: Trusted-Reference Formulas (FAO-56, USDA-NRCS, ASABE, IPCC, NRC)

all_formulas.name: Yield Gap
all_formulas.variables:
Y_potential = potential yield (variety × climate)
Y_actual = farmer's actual yield
all_formulas.purpose: Quantify unrealized yield — key metric for development programs.
all_formulas.example: Maize Y_potential=12 t/ha, actual=7 → YG = 5 t/ha (42% gap).
all_formulas.pitfall: Using record yield as potential — should be climate-adjusted.
all_formulas.decision: Close yield gap via: 30% nutrient, 25% water, 20% pest, 25% management.
all_formulas.notes: Source: FAO; GYGA (Global Yield Gap Atlas).
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تقدير الإنتاج غير المحقق.
all_formulas.part: Trusted-Reference Formulas (FAO-56, USDA-NRCS, ASABE, IPCC, NRC)

all_formulas.name: Harvest Index (HI)
all_formulas.variables:
Y_grain = grain yield (kg/ha)
Y_biomass = total aboveground biomass (kg/ha)
HI = 0 to 1
all_formulas.purpose: Partitioning efficiency — modern varieties HI 0.50; old 0.30.
all_formulas.example: Wheat: grain=6000, biomass=12000 → HI=0.50. Excellent.
all_formulas.pitfall: Including root biomass (changes HI dramatically).
all_formulas.decision: HI < 0.40: improve fertility, water, or disease control.
all_formulas.notes: Source: FAO; Donald & Hamblin (1976).
all_formulas.purpose_ar: كفاءة التقسيم بين الحبوب والكتلة الحيوية.
all_formulas.part: Trusted-Reference Formulas (FAO-56, USDA-NRCS, ASABE, IPCC, NRC)

all_formulas.name: Partial Budget Analysis
all_formulas.variables:
B_new = benefits of new practice
B_old = benefits of current
C_new = costs of new practice
C_old = costs of current
all_formulas.purpose: Evaluate if a management change is profitable.
all_formulas.example: New fertigation: B_new=$3000/ha, B_old=$2500. C_new=$700, C_old=$400. Net = 500-300 = $200/ha benefit.
all_formulas.pitfall: Forgetting opportunity cost; ignoring risk premium.
all_formulas.decision: Adopt if Net > 0 AND payback < 3 years.
all_formulas.notes: Source: USDA-NRCS; Kay & Edwards (2004).
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تقييم ربحية تغيير الإدارة.
all_formulas.part: Trusted-Reference Formulas (FAO-56, USDA-NRCS, ASABE, IPCC, NRC)

all_formulas.name: Body Condition Score Change
all_formulas.variables:
BCS_end = score at end (1-5)
BCS_start = score at start
weeks = observation period
all_formulas.purpose: Monitor energy balance in dairy cows — losing > 0.5 BCS/week is risky.
all_formulas.example: Fresh cow: BCS 3.5 → 3.0 in 4 weeks → change = -0.125/week (acceptable).
all_formulas.pitfall: Subjective scoring — use same trained scorer throughout.
all_formulas.decision: Lose > 0.5/wk: increase energy density; check ketosis.
all_formulas.notes: Source: Edmonson et al. (1989); NRC 2021.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: مراقبة توازن الطاقة في الأبقار.
all_formulas.part: Trusted-Reference Formulas (FAO-56, USDA-NRCS, ASABE, IPCC, NRC)

all_formulas.name: Water Quality Index (Aquaculture)
all_formulas.variables:
Wi = weight of parameter i
Qi = quality rating (0-100) of parameter i
DO, pH, T, NH₃, turbidity common parameters
all_formulas.purpose: Single metric for aquaculture water quality.
all_formulas.pitfall: Using wrong weights — calibrate to species tolerance.
all_formulas.decision: WQI < 70: water exchange. < 50: emergency harvest.
all_formulas.notes: Source: CCME (2001); Brown et al. (1970).
all_formulas.purpose_ar: مقياس واحد لجودة ماء الاستزراع السمكي.
all_formulas.part: Trusted-Reference Formulas (FAO-56, USDA-NRCS, ASABE, IPCC, NRC)

all_formulas.name: Rotational Grazing Rest Period
all_formulas.variables:
TR = total rest required (days)
n = number of paddocks
PD = paddock grazing duration (days)
all_formulas.purpose: Size rotational grazing system for sustainable forage use.
all_formulas.example: TR=30d, n=8, PD=3d → RP = 30/7 - 3 = 1.3d (too short — increase paddocks).
all_formulas.pitfall: Underestimating regrowth time in dry conditions.
all_formulas.decision: Adjust paddock count to give 25-40 days rest in temperate climates.
all_formulas.notes: Source: USDA-NRCS; Barnes et al. (2007) Forages.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تحديد نظام الرعي الدوار للاستخدام المستدام.
all_formulas.part: Trusted-Reference Formulas (FAO-56, USDA-NRCS, ASABE, IPCC, NRC)

all_formulas.name: Feed Conversion Ratio (FCR)
all_formulas.variables:
Feed_DM = feed dry matter intake (kg)
Weight_gain = animal weight gain (kg)
all_formulas.purpose: Efficiency of converting feed to animal mass — key economic metric.
all_formulas.example: Broiler: 3.0 kg feed → 1.6 kg gain → FCR = 1.875. Excellent.
all_formulas.pitfall: Using as-fed feed instead of DM; including mortality.
all_formulas.decision: Cattle FCR > 8: check parasites, genetics. Poultry > 2.2: disease check.
all_formulas.notes: Source: NRC (2021); FAO Animal Production.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: كفاءة تحويل العلف إلى كتلة حيوانية.
all_formulas.part: Trusted-Reference Formulas (FAO-56, USDA-NRCS, ASABE, IPCC, NRC)

all_formulas.name: Carbon Footprint per kg Product
all_formulas.variables:
Total_GHG = all emissions (kg CO₂e/ha)
Yield = product yield (kg/ha)
CF = kg CO₂e per kg product
all_formulas.purpose: Compare sustainability across production systems.
all_formulas.example: Wheat: 2000 kg CO₂e/ha / 6000 kg/ha = 0.33 kg CO₂e/kg wheat. Beef: 12000 / 800 = 15 kg CO₂e/kg.
all_formulas.pitfall: Forgetting soil carbon sequestration (net-zero possible).
all_formulas.decision: Benchmark: wheat <0.5, tomato <0.3, chicken <3, beef <20.
all_formulas.notes: Source: IPCC 2019; FAO SAFA.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: مقارنة الاستدامة عبر نظم الإنتاج.
all_formulas.part: Trusted-Reference Formulas (FAO-56, USDA-NRCS, ASABE, IPCC, NRC)

all_formulas.name: Sustainability Index (SAFA)
all_formulas.variables:
Econ = economic score (0-100)
Env = environmental score (0-100)
Social = social score (0-100)
Governance = governance score (0-100)
all_formulas.purpose: Holistic sustainability — FAO SAFA framework.
all_formulas.example: Econ=70, Env=55, Social=80, Gov=60 → SI = 66.3 (moderate).
all_formulas.pitfall: Weighting all 4 equally — adjust for stakeholder priorities.
all_formulas.decision: SI < 50: high-risk operation. > 75: leader.
all_formulas.notes: Source: FAO SAFA (2013) Sustainability Assessment of Food and Agriculture.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: استدامة شاملة — إطار SAFA.
all_formulas.part: Trusted-Reference Formulas (FAO-56, USDA-NRCS, ASABE, IPCC, NRC)

all_formulas.name: Soil Health Score (Cornell)
all_formulas.formula: SHS = (OC + AC + BS + pH + EC + ROT) / 6
all_formulas.variables:
OC = organic carbon score
AC = active carbon score
BS = base saturation score
pH = pH score
EC = biological activity
ROT = root health rating
Each 0-100
all_formulas.purpose: Comprehensive soil health — Cornell Comprehensive Assessment.
all_formulas.example: OC=60, AC=50, BS=80, pH=85, EC=70, ROT=75 → SHS=70 (good).
all_formulas.pitfall: Sampling only top 15cm — miss subsoil constraints.
all_formulas.decision: SHS <50: plant cover crop, reduce tillage, add compost.
all_formulas.notes: Source: Cornell Soil Health Lab (Moebius-Clune et al. 2016).
all_formulas.purpose_ar: صحة شاملة للتربة — تقييم كورنيل.
all_formulas.part: Trusted-Reference Formulas (FAO-56, USDA-NRCS, ASABE, IPCC, NRC)

all_formulas.name: Equilibrium Moisture Content (Henderson)
all_formulas.variables:
RH = decimal (0–1)
T = °C
A, B = crop-specific constants
all_formulas.purpose: Predict the final moisture content grain will reach when stored at a given temperature and humidity. Below 14% moisture, grain can be stored safely for months; above 18%, mold and mycotoxins develop rapidly.
all_formulas.pitfall: Each crop has different A, B constants. Using wheat constants for rice gives 2-3% error.
all_formulas.decision: Store grain only when actual moisture ≤ EMC at the storage environment's worst-case RH.
all_formulas.notes: Henderson equation is the simplest EMC model. Modified Henderson (Thompson 1968) and GAB (Guggenheim-Anderson-de Boer) are more accurate for engineering design.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: التنبؤ بمحتوى الرطوبة النهائي للحبوب عند درجة حرارة ورطوبة معينتين.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
RH = نسبة (0-1)
T = مئوية
A, B = ثوابت خاصة بالمحصول

all_formulas.name: Safe Storage Days (Fraser-Dua)
all_formulas.formula: log(D) = a − b × M − c × T
all_formulas.variables:
D = safe storage days
M = moisture content (% wet basis)
T = temperature (°C)
a, b, c = crop constants
all_formulas.purpose: Estimate how many days grain can be stored before visible mold or mycotoxin (aflatoxin) development. Below 5 days = high risk; above 100 days = safe.
all_formulas.example: Maize at 18% moisture, 25°C: a=8.5, b=0.35, c=0.12 → log(D)=8.5−0.35×18−0.12×25=1.4 → D≈25 days. Below 30 days: dry within 2 weeks.
all_formulas.pitfall: Aflatoxin can develop before visible mold. Add safety factor of 0.7× to computed days.
all_formulas.decision: If safe storage days < 30, dry grain within 2 weeks or cool the bin.
all_formulas.notes: Fraser & Dua (1976) for maize. Similar models exist for wheat (Sinha & Muir), rice (Seib), sorghum.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تقدير عدد الأيام التي يمكن تخزين الحبوب فيها قبل تطور العفن أو السموم الفطرية.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
D = أيام
M = رطوبة (%)
T = حرارة (مئوية)
a,b,c = ثوابت

all_formulas.name: Thin-Layer Drying Rate (Page Equation)
all_formulas.variables:
MR = moisture ratio = (M − Me)/(M0 − Me)
t = time (hours)
k, n = drying constants
all_formulas.purpose: Predict grain moisture at any time during thin-layer drying (depth < 0.5 m). Used to size batch dryers and estimate drying time.
all_formulas.pitfall: k and n depend strongly on air temperature — doubling air temp roughly quadruples k.
all_formulas.decision: For batch drying: target 2-3% above EMC to avoid over-drying (wastes energy + cracks grain).
all_formulas.notes: Page (1949) is the most widely used thin-layer model. Other models: Lewis (simpler), Midilli (more accurate for high-temp).
all_formulas.purpose_ar: التنبؤ برطوبة الحبوب في أي وقت أثناء التجفيف الطبقي الرقيق.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
MR = نسبة الرطوبة
t = وقت (ساعة)
k,n = ثوابت

all_formulas.name: Drying Energy Cost ($/t)
all_formulas.variables:
V_w = water removed (kg/t)
h_fg = latent heat vaporization (~2260 kJ/kg)
P_e = electricity price ($/kWh)
η = dryer efficiency (0.4–0.7)
all_formulas.purpose: Estimate energy cost per tonne of grain dried. Used to compare drying options and decide whether to wait for field drying vs. artificial dry.
all_formulas.pitfall: η varies widely — low-temp dryers (0.6-0.7) vs. high-temp (0.4-0.5). Solar dryers have η=0 but capital cost.
all_formulas.decision: If drying cost > 5% of grain value, consider field drying (natural) or low-temp bin drying.
all_formulas.notes: Latent heat varies slightly with grain temp; use 2260 kJ/kg as standard. Gas-fired dryers substitute fuel cost.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تقدير تكلفة الطاقة لكل طن من الحبوب المجففة.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
V_w = ماء مزال (كجم/طن)
h_fg = حرارة تبخر
P_e = سعر الكهرباء
η = كفاءة المجفف

all_formulas.name: Bin Aeration Fan Sizing (CFM)
all_formulas.variables:
AFR = airflow rate (CFM/bu or m³/min/t)
grain_weight = bushels or tonnes in bin
all_formulas.purpose: Size the aeration fan for a grain bin. Aeration cools grain, prevents moisture migration, and extends safe storage. Minimum AFR = 0.1 CFM/bu for cooling; 1.0+ CFM/bu for drying.
all_formulas.example: 1000 bu wheat bin, cooling only: CFM = 0.1 × 1000 = 100 CFM. For drying at 1.5 CFM/bu: 1500 CFM.
all_formulas.pitfall: Static pressure increases with grain depth + density. Use bin manufacturer's pressure chart to select fan horsepower.
all_formulas.decision: Cool grain within 1 month of harvest — even dry grain spoils if stored warm (>20°C).
all_formulas.notes: ASABE Standard D272 gives pressure-drop curves by grain type. 1 CFM/bu ≈ 1.06 m³/min/t.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تحديد حجم مروحة التهوية لصومعة حبوب.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
AFR = معدل تدفق الهواء
grain_weight = وزن الحبوب

all_formulas.name: Grain Respiration Heat (kcal/t/day)
all_formulas.variables:
M = moisture (% wet basis)
T = temperature (°C)
all_formulas.purpose: Estimate metabolic heat produced by grain respiration. Above 2 kcal/t/day, the grain is spoiling — heat accumulation accelerates mold and creates hot spots.
all_formulas.example: Maize at 18% moisture, 25°C: Q = 6.74 × 18^2.55 × 10^1.15 × 24 = 6.74 × 1430 × 14.1 × 24 ≈ very high — dry immediately.
all_formulas.pitfall: Respiration is self-accelerating: heat → mold → more heat. Monitor bin temp daily at multiple probes.
all_formulas.decision: If Q > 5 kcal/t/day, turn on aeration fans immediately + core the bin (remove center).
all_formulas.notes: Steele & Saul (1968). At 14% moisture, respiration is negligible. Above 18%, it's exponential.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تقدير الحرارة الأيضية الناتجة عن تنفس الحبوب.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
M = رطوبة (%)
T = حرارة (مئوية)

all_formulas.name: Shelf-Life Prediction (Arrhenius)
all_formulas.variables:
t₁, t₂ = shelf life at temps T₁, T₂
Q10 = temperature coefficient (typically 2–3)
all_formulas.purpose: Predict how shelf life changes with storage temperature. Critical for cold chain management of fruits, vegetables, and processed foods.
all_formulas.example: Tomatoes last 14 days at 4°C. At 20°C (16° warmer, Q10=2.5): t = 14 × 2.5^(−1.6) = 14 × 0.16 = 2.2 days. Room-temp shelf life is 6× shorter.
all_formulas.pitfall: Q10 varies by product (2 for grains, 2.5-3 for fresh produce, 3-4 for frozen). Some foods have non-Arrhenius behavior near freezing.
all_formulas.decision: Every 10°C reduction in storage temp roughly doubles shelf life for most fresh produce.
all_formulas.notes: Q10 model is an approximation. For precise work, use Arrhenius equation: k = A × exp(−Ea/RT).
all_formulas.purpose_ar: التنبؤ بكيفية تغير مدة الصلاحية مع درجة حرارة التخزين.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
t₁, t₂ = مدة الصلاحية
T₁, T₂ = درجة الحرارة
Q10 = معامل الحرارة

all_formulas.name: Cold Storage Refrigeration Load (tons)
all_formulas.variables:
Q_transmission = U × A × ΔT (W)
Q_product = m × cp × ΔT / t (W)
Q_infiltration = 0.5 × V × ΔH × n / 3600 (W)
Q_internal = lights + people + equipment (W)
3.517 = kW per refrigeration ton
all_formulas.purpose: Size refrigeration equipment for cold storage rooms. Critical for produce coolers, dairy, meat, and processed food storage.
all_formulas.example: 50 m³ cooler at 2°C, ambient 30°C: walls R-4 (U=0.25), area 80 m² → Q_trans=0.25×80×28=560 W. Product 500 kg apples 20°C→2°C in 12h: 500×3.8×18/43200=0.79 kW. Infiltration ~300 W. Lights+people ~200 W. Total ≈ 1.85 kW ≈ 0.53 tons.
all_formulas.pitfall: Infiltration load can dominate if door opens frequently. Add 20% safety factor.
all_formulas.decision: Use 2-3× peak load for equipment sizing to allow pulldown after door openings.
all_formulas.notes: ASHRAE Fundamentals Ch 24. For produce, also factor in respiration heat (see PH.6).
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تحديد معدات التبريد لغرف التخزين البارد.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
Q = مكونات الحمل (واط)
3.517 = تحويل kW إلى طن تبريد

all_formulas.name: Modified Atmosphere Storage Gas Mix
all_formulas.variables:
R_O₂ = crop O₂ consumption (mL/kg/h)
W = product mass (kg)
V = free volume in container (L)
t = time (h)
all_formulas.purpose: Design controlled atmosphere (CA) or modified atmosphere (MA) storage. Low O₂ (2-5%) + elevated CO₂ (5-15%) extends shelf life of apples, pears, berries 2-10×.
all_formulas.example: Apples: R_O₂ = 8 mL/kg/h at 0°C. 1000 kg in 1500 L free volume. O₂ drops from 21% to 3% in: t = −(1500×0.21)/(8×1000) × ln(0.03/0.21) ≈ 63 hours.
all_formulas.pitfall: Anaerobic conditions (<1% O₂) cause fermentation + off-flavors. Monitor O₂ continuously.
all_formulas.decision: Use CA for long-term storage (apples 6-12 months). Use MA films for short-term transit.
all_formulas.notes: Each crop has optimal O₂/CO₂/N₂ ratio. Apples: 2% O₂ / 2% CO₂. Lettuce: 3% O₂ / 5% CO₂.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تصميم تخزين الجو المعدل أو المسيطر عليه لإطالة مدة الصلاحية.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
R_O₂ = استهلاك الأكسجين
W = كتلة المنتج
V = حجم حر

all_formulas.name: Ethylene Production Rate (µL/kg/h)
all_formulas.variables:
E₀ = baseline ethylene at 20°C (µL/kg/h)
Q10 = 2–3 for most climacteric fruits
t = storage time (days)
k = senescence rate (0.01–0.1/day)
all_formulas.purpose: Predict ethylene accumulation in storage. Climacteric fruits (apples, bananas, tomatoes, avocados) produce ethylene that accelerates ripening of nearby produce. 0.1 ppm ethylene can halve shelf life.
all_formulas.example: Apples at 0°C: E₀=100 µL/kg/h, Q10=2.8. E = 100 × 2.8^((0−20)/10) = 100 × 2.8^(−2) = 100 × 0.128 = 12.8 µL/kg/h. Still significant — ventilate or scrub.
all_formulas.pitfall: Mixing ethylene producers (apples) with ethylene-sensitive crops (carrots, lettuce, flowers) causes rapid quality loss.
all_formulas.decision: Store ethylene producers separately. Use KMnO₄ ethylene scrubbers in CA rooms.
all_formulas.notes: Kader (2002) Postharvest Technology. Non-climacteric fruits (citrus, grapes, strawberries) produce <0.1 µL/kg/h.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: التنبؤ بتراكم الإيثيلين في التخزين وتأثيره على النضج.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
E₀ = خط الأساس
Q10 = معامل الحرارة
t = وقت التخزين

all_formulas.name: Heating Load (BTU/hr or kW)
all_formulas.variables:
U = glazing U-value (W/m²/°C)
A = surface area (m²)
ΔT = inside − outside temp (°C)
infiltration = 0.1–0.3 for single glazing, 0.05 for double
all_formulas.purpose: Size greenhouse heating system. Critical for winter production in cold climates — undersized heaters mean frozen crops.
all_formulas.example: 500 m² greenhouse, single poly (U=6.5), inside 18°C, outside −5°C: Q = 6.5 × 500 × 23 × 1.2 = 89.7 kW ≈ 306 kBTU/hr. Need ~100 kW heater.
all_formulas.pitfall: U-value depends on glazing: single glass=6.5, double poly=3.5, polycarbonate twin-wall=2.5, triple-wall=1.8.
all_formulas.decision: Add 20% safety factor for wind + edge effects. Thermal screens reduce load by 30-50%.
all_formulas.notes: ASAE Standards EP406. Ground heat loss (10-15% of total) often neglected in simple calcs.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تحديد نظام تدفئة البيت المحمي للإنتاج الشتوي.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
U = معامل نقل الحرارة
A = المساحة
ΔT = فرق الحرارة

all_formulas.name: Ventilation Rate (Summer Cooling)
all_formulas.variables:
V = ventilation rate (m³/s)
Q_solar = solar heat gain (W)
ρ = air density (1.2 kg/m³)
cp = specific heat (1005 J/kg/°C)
ΔT = allowable temp rise above ambient
all_formulas.purpose: Size exhaust fans for summer cooling. Without adequate ventilation, greenhouse temps exceed 50°C and kill crops.
all_formulas.example: 500 m² greenhouse, 70% solar transmission: Q_solar = 500 × 600 × 0.7 = 210 kW. Allow 5°C rise: V = 210000/(1.2×1005×5) = 34.8 m³/s = 73,700 CFM. Use 3 fans × 25,000 CFM each.
all_formulas.pitfall: Solar load = 600 W/m² on clear day. Shade cloth (50%) reduces this by half.
all_formulas.decision: Standard: 1 air change per minute (ACM) for summer. 0.25-0.5 ACM for winter dehumidification.
all_formulas.notes: Add 15% for fan static pressure. Use HAF (horizontal airflow) fans to mix air within greenhouse.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تحديد مراوح العادم للتبريد الصيفي للبيت المحمي.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
V = معدل التهوية
Q_solar = حرارة شمسية
ΔT = ارتفاع الحرارة المسموح

all_formulas.name: CO₂ Enrichment Rate (kg/hr)
all_formulas.formula: CO₂_rate = (C_target − C_ambient) × V_greenhouse × ρ × n / (1e6 × t)
all_formulas.variables:
C_target = target CO₂ ppm (1000–1500)
C_ambient = 400 ppm
V = greenhouse volume (m³)
ρ = air density (1.2 kg/m³)
n = air changes per hour
t = 1 hour
all_formulas.purpose: Size CO₂ generation or supply system. Enrichment to 1000-1500 ppm increases yield 20-30% in tomatoes, cucumbers, lettuce. Only effective when vents are closed (winter).
all_formulas.example: 500 m² × 4m height = 2000 m³. Target 1000 ppm, 0.5 air changes/hr: CO₂ = (1000−400)×2000×1.2×0.5/(1e6×1) = 0.72 kg CO₂/hr. Burn 0.5 L propane/hr or use liquid CO₂ tank.
all_formulas.pitfall: CO₂ above 1500 ppm provides no additional benefit and is hazardous to workers above 5000 ppm.
all_formulas.decision: Stop enrichment when vents open >10% — wastes CO₂. Use only during photosynthesis hours (sunrise to sunset).
all_formulas.notes: 1 kg CO₂ = 0.55 m³ gas. Combustion: 1 L propane produces 1.5 kg CO₂. Burners also produce heat + water vapor.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تحديد نظام توليد أو تزويد CO₂ لزيادة الإنتاجية.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
C = تركيز CO₂ (ppm)
V = حجم البيت
n = تغييرات الهواء/ساعة

all_formulas.name: Fogging System Sizing (L/hr)
all_formulas.formula: W = V × ρ × (x_out − x_in) × n × 3600 / h_fg
all_formulas.variables:
V = greenhouse volume (m³)
ρ = 1.2 kg/m³
x = humidity ratio (kg water/kg dry air)
n = air changes per second
h_fg = latent heat (2260 kJ/kg)
all_formulas.purpose: Size fogging (mist) system for evaporative cooling + humidity control. Fine droplets (<50 microns) evaporate before hitting plants, cooling air without wetting foliage.
all_formulas.example: 2000 m³ greenhouse, drop from 35°C/30% RH to 28°C/70% RH: Δx = 0.012 kg/kg. W = 2000×1.2×0.012×0.5/2260×3600 ≈ 23 L/hr. Use 50 nozzles × 0.5 L/hr each.
all_formulas.pitfall: High-pressure fogging (>50 bar) produces fine droplets but is expensive. Low-pressure (<10 bar) wets foliage — disease risk.
all_formulas.decision: Use fogging only with HAF fans for circulation. Stops when RH >85% (disease threshold).
all_formulas.notes: Evaporative cooling is adiabatic — drops sensible heat, raises latent heat. Pad-and-fan is simpler alternative for dry climates.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تحديد نظام الضباب للتبريد التبخيري والتحكم في الرطوبة.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
V = الحجم
x = نسبة الرطوبة
h_fg = حرارة التبخر

all_formulas.name: Thermal Screen Fuel Savings (%)
all_formulas.variables:
R_screen = R-value of screen (m²·°C/W)
R_glazing = R-value of glazing
Typical screens: R=0.4 to 0.8
all_formulas.purpose: Estimate fuel savings from night-time thermal screen. Screens are the single most cost-effective greenhouse energy retrofit — 30-50% heating reduction.
all_formulas.example: Single poly glazing R=0.15, add R=0.5 screen: Savings = 0.5/(0.5+0.15) × 100 = 77%. Real-world ~50% due to imperfect sealing.
all_formulas.pitfall: Screens must close completely. 10% gap = 50% savings lost.
all_formulas.decision: Open screen 30 min before sunrise to prevent humidity spike + condensation drip.
all_formulas.notes: Aluminized screens reflect long-wave radiation back to crop. Black screens absorb — use only for blackout (photoperiod).
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تقدير توفير الوقود من الستائر الحرارية الليلية.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
R = قيمة العزل
screen = الستارة
glazing = التغطية

all_formulas.name: Light Transmission (%)
all_formulas.variables:
τ_glazing = single glass 0.9, double poly 0.75, polycarbonate 0.80
τ_structure = 0.85 (typical)
τ_screen = 0.85 (open) to 0.45 (closed)
θ = angle of incidence
all_formulas.purpose: Calculate light reaching crops. Light is the #1 yield driver — 1% more light = 1% more yield for most greenhouse crops (rule of thumb).
all_formulas.example: Double poly greenhouse, no screen, winter sun at 45°: τ = 0.75 × 0.85 × 1.0 × cos(45°) = 0.45. Only 45% of outdoor light reaches crop.
all_formulas.pitfall: Dust on glazing reduces transmission 5-15% — wash quarterly.
all_formulas.decision: For winter production, supplement with HPS or LED grow lights to reach 200 µmol/m²/s minimum at canopy.
all_formulas.notes: Cos(θ) factor is for direct beam. For diffuse light, transmission is roughly constant. Diffuse glazing (etched glass) improves light distribution.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: حساب الضوء الذي يصل إلى المحصول — العامل الأول للإنتاجية.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
τ = معامل النفاذية
θ = زاوية السقوط

all_formulas.name: Thermal Mass (Water Wall Sizing)
all_formulas.variables:
Q_night = night heat demand (kJ)
ρ = 1000 kg/m³
cp = 4.18 kJ/kg/°C
ΔT = allowable water temp drop (°C)
all_formulas.purpose: Size passive thermal mass (water tanks) to store daytime solar heat for night-time heating. Eliminates or reduces heating fuel in mild climates.
all_formulas.example: 100 MJ night heat demand, allow 15°C water drop: V = 100000/(1000×4.18×15) = 1.6 m³. Use 2× 1000 L IBC totes painted black.
all_formulas.pitfall: Thermal mass only works if greenhouse is well-insulated. Cold-climate greenhouses still need backup heat.
all_formulas.decision: Water has 4× the volumetric heat capacity of rock. Place mass on north wall (no shading).
all_formulas.notes: Compost piles also serve as thermal mass — generate heat from microbial activity + store solar.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تحديد الكتلة الحرارية السلبية لتخزين حرارة النهار للتدفئة الليلية.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
Q = الطلب الحراري الليلي
ρ = كثافة الماء
cp = حرارة نوعية

all_formulas.name: Photosynthetic Photon Flux (PPF) Requirement
all_formulas.variables:
DLI = Daily Light Integral (mol/m²/day)
PPFD_avg = average photon flux (µmol/m²/s)
t_light = light hours per day (seconds)
all_formulas.purpose: Calculate supplemental lighting needs. Target DLI: 12-17 for leafy greens, 17-22 for tomatoes, 25+ for cucumbers. Below target → slow growth + poor yield.
all_formulas.example: Tomatoes need DLI 22. Winter greenhouse gets DLI 5. Need supplement: PPFD = (22−5)×1e6/(16×3600) = 295 µmol/m²/s. Use 4× 600W HPS lights per 100 m².
all_formulas.pitfall: DLI is for photons (400-700 nm), not all light. Lux-to-PPFD conversion: PPFD ≈ lux / 54 for sunlight, / 82 for HPS.
all_formulas.decision: LEDs use 40-60% less electricity than HPS for same PPFD. Payback 3-5 years.
all_formulas.notes: Photoperiod + DLI both matter. Long-day plants (spinach) need >12 hr. Short-day (chrysanthemum) need <12 hr to flower.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: حساب احتياجات الإضاءة التكميلية للإنتاج الشتوي.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
DLI = اليومي للضوء
PPFD = كثافة تدفق الفوتونات
t = ساعات الضوء

all_formulas.name: C:N Ratio Mixer (Two Feedstocks)
all_formulas.variables:
C₁, C₂ = carbon % of each feedstock
N₁, N₂ = nitrogen %
W₁, W₂ = weights (kg)
all_formulas.purpose: Calculate C:N ratio when mixing two feedstocks. Target 30:1 for optimal composting — below 20:1 loses N as ammonia, above 40:1 is too slow.
all_formulas.example: Mix 100 kg grass clippings (C:N=15:1) with 50 kg leaves (C:N=60:1): C:N = (45×100 + 48×50)/(3×100 + 0.8×50) = 6900/340 = 20.3:1. Too low — add more leaves.
all_formulas.pitfall: Carbon must be biodegradable. Wood chips have C:N 400:1 but only 30% available — use 130:1 effective.
all_formulas.decision: Aim 25-30:1 initially. C:N drops during composting — final mature compost is 15-20:1.
all_formulas.notes: For 3+ feedstocks: C:N = Σ(Cᵢ×Wᵢ) / Σ(Nᵢ×Wᵢ). Online calculators + spreadsheet templates exist.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: حساب نسبة C:N عند خلط مادتين للتسميد.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
C = كربون (%)
N = نيتروجين (%)
W = وزن (كجم)

all_formulas.name: Moisture Adjustment (Water to Add)
all_formulas.variables:
W_dry = dry weight of pile (kg)
M_target = target moisture (0.55–0.65)
M_current = current moisture (decimal)
all_formulas.purpose: Calculate water needed to reach 55-65% moisture — the optimal range for composting. Below 40%, microbes go dormant; above 70%, pile goes anaerobic.
all_formulas.example: 500 kg pile at 35% moisture, target 60%: W_add = 500×0.65×(0.60−0.35)/(1−0.60) = 203 L water.
all_formulas.pitfall: Pile moisture varies — sample from 5+ locations. Use squeeze test: should feel like wrung-out sponge.
all_formulas.decision: Cover pile with tarp in rainy season to prevent waterlogging. Turn pile to add air if moisture >70%.
all_formulas.notes: Green feedstocks (grass, food waste) are 80-90% moisture. Brown (leaves, straw) are 10-20%. Mix achieves target.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: حساب الماء اللازم للوصول إلى رطوبة 55-65% المثلى.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
W_dry = الوزن الجاف
M = الرطوبة (نسبة)

all_formulas.name: Compost Maturity Index
all_formulas.variables:
T_max = max temperature reached (°C)
days_above_55°C = pathogen-kill days
final_C:N = C:N of finished compost
all_formulas.purpose: Estimate compost maturity (stability). MI > 5 = mature; 2-5 = curing needed; < 2 = immature (will tie up N in soil).
all_formulas.example: Pile reached 65°C for 7 days, final C:N=18: MI = (65×7)/(18×10) = 2.5. Curing needed — let sit 4 more weeks.
all_formulas.pitfall: MI is a rough guide. Confirm with Solvita CO₂ burst test (<5 mg CO₂-C/g = stable) or germination test (>80% seedling emergence in compost extract).
all_formulas.decision: Mature compost: dark, crumbly, earthy smell, no ammonia. Use immediately. Immature: use only as mulch, not in potting mix.
all_formulas.notes: US Composting Council STA seal requires: C:N < 25, pH 5.5-8.5, salts < 6 dS/m, heavy metals below EPA limits.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تقدير نضج السماد — ضروري قبل التطبيق على المحاصيل.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
T = الحرارة
days = أيام فوق 55°
C:N = النسبة النهائية

all_formulas.name: N Mineralization Rate (%/year)
all_formulas.variables:
N_total = total N in compost (kg/t)
T = mean annual soil temp (°C)
years = 1, 2, 3...
all_formulas.purpose: Estimate N available to crops from compost. Year 1: ~10% releases. Year 2: +5%. Year 3: +2%. Compost builds soil N reserve — slow release.
all_formulas.example: Compost with 15 kg N/t, soil temp 18°C, Year 1: N_avail = 15 × (0.10 + 0.05×8) = 15 × 0.5 = 7.5 kg N/t. Apply 20 t/ha → 150 kg N/ha available Year 1.
all_formulas.pitfall: Mineralization depends on soil moisture + biology. Dry/cold soils release <5%. Tropical soils: 20-30%.
all_formulas.decision: Don't count compost as sole N source for Year 1. Supplement with mineral N or legume cover crop.
all_formulas.notes: Adjust per compost type: solid manure 30-40% Year 1, composted manure 10-15%, vermicompost 25-35%.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تقدير النيتروجين المتاح للمحاصيل من السماد العضوي.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
N_total = إجمالي N
T = حرارة التربة
years = السنوات

all_formulas.name: Bulk Density + Porosity
all_formulas.variables:
ρ_bulk = pile bulk density (typically 400-600 kg/m³)
ρ_particle = particle density (≈ 1600 kg/m³ for organic matter)
all_formulas.purpose: Calculate air-filled porosity for aeration. Composting needs >30% porosity for oxygen penetration. Below 20%, pile goes anaerobic.
all_formulas.example: Pile bulk density 500 kg/m³: Porosity = 1 − (500/1600) = 0.69 = 69%. Excellent — well-aerated.
all_formulas.pitfall: Compaction reduces porosity over time. Turn pile every 7-10 days for first 3 weeks to restore porosity.
all_formulas.decision: If porosity <30%: add bulky material (wood chips, straw) at 1:3 ratio by volume.
all_formulas.notes: Free air space (FAS) = porosity − moisture. Target 35-50% FAS for active composting.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: حساب المسامية للتهوية — ضرورية للتسميد الهوائي.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
ρ_bulk = الكثافة الظاهرية
ρ_particle = كثافة الجسيمات

all_formulas.name: Compost Tea Recipe (per 100 L)
all_formulas.formula: Compost : Molasses : Humic : Kelp = 2 : 0.5 : 0.1 : 0.1 (kg per 100 L water)
all_formulas.variables:
Compost = mature, vermicompost preferred
Molasses = food for microbes
Humic acid = microbial habitat
Kelp = trace minerals + growth hormones
all_formulas.purpose: Brew aerobic compost tea — liquid biological amendment. Active microbes suppress disease + solubilize nutrients when sprayed on leaves or soil.
all_formulas.example: 100 L brew: 2 kg vermicompost + 0.5 kg molasses + 0.1 kg humic + 0.1 kg kelp. Brew 24 hr with aquarium pump (≥5 L air/min).
all_formulas.pitfall: Anaerobic tea (no aeration) grows human pathogens (E. coli, Salmonella). Use within 4 hr of brewing.
all_formulas.decision: Apply as foliar spray at 1:5 dilution, or soil drench at 1:2. Best applied at dawn/dusk.
all_formulas.notes: Beneficial when microbial diversity is high. Test with microscope — should see bacteria, fungi, protozoa, nematodes.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تحضير شاي السماد الهوائي — مكمل بيولوجي سائل.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
Compost = سماد ناضج
Molasses = غذاء الميكروبات
Humic = حمض هيوميك

all_formulas.name: VRA Prescription Rate (N from NDVI)
all_formulas.variables:
N_max = max N rate (kg/ha)
NDVI_zone = mean NDVI in management zone
NDVI_max = NDVI of healthiest zone
N_min = baseline N (30-50 kg/ha)
all_formulas.purpose: Generate variable-rate nitrogen prescription from NDVI zones. Low NDVI (stressed) gets more N; high NDVI (healthy) gets less. Saves 15-30% N without yield loss.
all_formulas.pitfall: NDVI saturates above 0.8 — can't distinguish vigorous from very vigorous. Use NDRE (red edge) for high-biomass crops.
all_formulas.decision: Apply VRA only if field has >30% NDVI variability. Uniform fields: use flat rate.
all_formulas.notes: Sensor-based (real-time) vs. map-based (prescription). Map-based is simpler; sensor-based is more accurate.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: توليد وصفة نيتروجين متغيرة من مناطق NDVI.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
N_max = أقصى معدل
NDVI = مؤشر الغطاء النباتي
N_min = الحد الأدنى

all_formulas.name: NDVI Threshold Classifier
all_formulas.formula: Zone_i = { NDVI < T_low: 'Critical', T_low ≤ NDVI < T_high: 'Stressed', NDVI ≥ T_high: 'Healthy' }
all_formulas.variables:
T_low = lower threshold (typically 0.3–0.4)
T_high = upper threshold (typically 0.6–0.7)
all_formulas.purpose: Classify NDVI values into management zones for variable rate + scouting prioritization. Generates 3-zone map: critical (red), stressed (yellow), healthy (green).
all_formulas.example: Wheat field: T_low=0.35, T_high=0.65. 35% of field < 0.35 → critical zone (apply more N + scout for disease). 50% in middle → stressed. 15% > 0.65 → healthy.
all_formulas.pitfall: Thresholds are crop + stage specific. Use histogram of field NDVI to find natural breaks (Jenks classification).
all_formulas.decision: Scout critical zones first (pests? disease? compaction?). Sample stressed zones for tissue test.
all_formulas.notes: For advanced: k-means clustering on multi-temporal NDVI identifies stable management zones across seasons.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تصنيف قيم NDVI إلى مناطق إدارة للتطبيق المتغير والكشف.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
T_low = العتبة الدنيا
T_high = العتبة العليا

all_formulas.name: Yield Monitor Calibration (Mass Flow)
all_formulas.variables:
CF_moisture = (100 − M_monitor) / (100 − M_standard)
CF_flow = actual_weight / monitor_weight
CF_lag = GPS time delay correction
all_formulas.purpose: Correct raw yield monitor data for moisture, flow rate, and GPS lag. Uncorrected data overstates yield by 5-15%.
all_formulas.example: Monitor reads 10 t/ha at 25% moisture, actual 14% standard. CF_moisture = (100−25)/(100−14) = 0.87. Flow test shows monitor 8% high: CF_flow = 1/1.08 = 0.93. Corrected: 10×0.87×0.93 = 8.1 t/ha.
all_formulas.pitfall: Calibrate per crop + per moisture range. Yield monitor needs 6-8 calibration loads spanning expected flow rates.
all_formulas.decision: Recalibrate if harvest conditions change (wet → dry, or variety change).
all_formulas.notes: ASABE Standard X587. Test weight (kg/hL) also affects accuracy — input manually per field.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تصحيح بيانات مراقب الإنتاج الخام للرطوبة والتدفق وتأخر GPS.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
CF = معامل التصحيح
M = الرطوبة

all_formulas.name: Optimal Grid Sampling Density
all_formulas.variables:
A = field area (m²)
range = spatial correlation range from semivariogram (m)
all_formulas.purpose: Determine optimal soil sampling density based on spatial variability. Uniform fields need fewer samples; variable fields need more. Saves $5-15/ha vs. fixed grid.
all_formulas.example: 10 ha field, semivariogram range=60 m: N = 100000/(2×3600)+4 = 17.9 → 18 samples. ~1 sample per 0.55 ha.
all_formulas.pitfall: Semivariogram requires prior grid sampling (chicken + egg). Start with 1 ha grid, refine Year 2.
all_formulas.decision: Zone sampling (3-5 composites per zone) is more cost-effective than grid sampling for most fields.
all_formulas.notes: Standard grids: 1 ha (intensive), 2.5 ha (standard), 5 ha (extensive). Cost: $10-25 per sample.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تحديد كثافة أخذ عينات التربة المثلى بناءً على التباين المكاني.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
A = المساحة
range = مدى الارتباط المكاني

all_formulas.name: Prescription Map Generation (Shapefile)
all_formulas.variables:
Zone(x,y) = management zone at GPS point
RateTable = { zone1: rate1, zone2: rate2, ... }
all_formulas.purpose: Generate prescription (Rx) map for variable-rate equipment. Shapefile with rate per polygon — loaded into controller for auto-rate-change.
all_formulas.example: 3 zones: A=140 kg N/ha, B=100, C=60. Export as shapefile with 'RATE' attribute. VR controller reads rate as tractor enters each zone polygon.
all_formulas.pitfall: Controller latency (2-5 sec) means rate changes lag GPS by 10-20 m. Add 'look-ahead' buffer.
all_formulas.decision: Use 12-row swath + section control to avoid double-application at headlands.
all_formulas.notes: ISO 11783 (ISOBUS) standard connects GPS, display, and rate controller. Older equipment needs aftermarket controller.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: توليد خريطة وصفة لمعدات التطبيق المتغير.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
Zone = منطقة الإدارة
RateTable = جدول المعدلات

all_formulas.name: Section Control Turn-On/Off Distance
all_formulas.variables:
v = ground speed (m/s)
t_latency = valve + GPS response time (2-5 s)
d_GPS_offset = GPS antenna to boom tip distance (m)
all_formulas.purpose: Calculate when to toggle sections at headlands to avoid skips (off too late) + overlaps (off too early). Saves 5-12% input cost.
all_formulas.example: Sprayer at 12 km/h (3.3 m/s), latency 3 s, GPS offset 2 m: d = 3.3×3 + 2 = 11.9 m. Toggle section 12 m before headland.
all_formulas.pitfall: Latency varies by valve type — pneumatic (1-2 s) vs. electric (3-5 s).
all_formulas.decision: Configure controller with measured latency + GPS offset. Test in open field with visible foam marker.
all_formulas.notes: Modern auto-steer + section control systems auto-compensate. Older systems need manual calibration.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: حساب وقت تشغيل/إيقاف الأقسام لتجنب الفجوات والتداخل.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
v = السرعة
t = زمن الاستجابة
d = إزاحة GPS

all_formulas.name: Kostiakov Infiltration Model
all_formulas.variables:
I(t) = cumulative infiltration (mm)
t = time since ponding (min)
k, a = soil-specific constants
all_formulas.purpose: Predict cumulative water infiltration into soil over time. Used for furrow + border irrigation design + runoff prediction.
all_formulas.pitfall: Kostiakov predicts I→0 rate at long times (unrealistic). Modified Kostiakov adds steady-state term: I = k×t^a + f0×t.
all_formulas.decision: If infiltration rate <5 mm/hr, install drainage. If >50 mm/hr, consider drip (basin/furrow wastes water).
all_formulas.notes: k, a from double-ring infiltrometer test. Typical: sand k=50 a=0.4, loam k=15 a=0.6, clay k=5 a=0.7.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: التنبؤ بالتراكم التراكمي للمياه في التربة بمرور الوقت.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
I = الترشيح التراكمي
t = الوقت
k, a = ثوابت

all_formulas.name: Horton Infiltration Model
all_formulas.variables:
f(t) = infiltration rate (mm/hr)
fc = steady-state infiltration rate
f0 = initial rate (at t=0)
k = decay constant
all_formulas.purpose: Model infiltration rate decay over time — starts high (dry soil), declines to steady state (saturated). Better than Kostiakov for long durations.
all_formulas.pitfall: f0 depends on antecedent moisture. After rain, f0 is much lower than for dry soil.
all_formulas.decision: Design irrigation sets so duration < time to reach fc. Otherwise, water runs off.
all_formulas.notes: Horton (1940). Alternative: Green-Ampt model with explicit physics (Darcy's law + sharp wetting front).
all_formulas.purpose_ar: نمذجة انخفاض معدل الترشيح مع الوقت — من الجاف إلى المشبع.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
f = معدل الترشيح
fc = المعدل المستقر
f0 = المعدل الأولي

all_formulas.name: Van Genuchten Soil Water Characteristic Curve
all_formulas.variables:
θ(h) = water content at matric potential h
θr = residual water content
θs = saturated water content
α, n, m = van Genuchten parameters
m = 1 − 1/n
all_formulas.purpose: Describe soil water retention — the relationship between water content and matric potential. Foundational for irrigation scheduling, drainage design, and root water uptake models.
all_formulas.pitfall: Parameters must be measured (tempe cells) or estimated via Rosetta pedotransfer functions from texture + bulk density.
all_formulas.decision: Field capacity ≈ h=−330 cm. Wilting point ≈ h=−15000 cm. Available water = θ(FC) − θ(PWP).
all_formulas.notes: Van Genuchten (1980). Most widely used model in HYDRUS, SWAT, and other soil-water models.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: وصف الاحتفاظ بماء التربة — العلاقة بين المحتوى المائي والجهد المصفوفي.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
θ = المحتوى المائي
θr = المتبقي
θs = المشبع
α, n, m = معاملات

all_formulas.name: Saturated Hydraulic Conductivity (Rosetta)
all_formulas.variables:
%sand, %silt, %clay = USDA texture
θ33 = water content at −33 kPa
θ1500 = water content at −1500 kPa
ρb = bulk density (g/cm³)
all_formulas.purpose: Estimate Ks (saturated hydraulic conductivity) from easily-measured soil properties. Ks determines drainage rate, irrigation set sizing, and groundwater recharge.
all_formulas.example: Sandy loam: 60% sand, 30% silt, 10% clay, ρb=1.4. Rosetta class 3 (texture + bulk density): Ks ≈ 50 mm/hr. Confirms well-drained soil.
all_formulas.pitfall: Rosetta has ±order-of-magnitude uncertainty. For design work, measure Ks directly (constant-head permeameter).
all_formulas.decision: Ks > 50 mm/hr: free-draining, suitable for drip. Ks 5-50: most crops. Ks < 5: install drainage.
all_formulas.notes: Rosetta is a pedotransfer function (PTF) — predicts hard-to-measure properties from easy-to-measure ones. Schaap + Leij (1998).
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تقدير Ks من خصائص التربة سهلة القياس.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
%sand = الرمل
%clay = الطين
ρb = الكثافة الظاهرية

all_formulas.name: Pore Size Distribution
all_formulas.variables:
d = equivalent pore diameter (µm)
h = matric potential (cm H₂O)
all_formulas.purpose: Calculate pore sizes from soil water characteristic. Macropores (>75 µm) drain at field capacity. Micropores (<0.2 µm) hold water at wilting point.
all_formulas.example: At field capacity (h=−330 cm): d = 3000/330 = 9 µm. Pores > 9 µm are drained. At wilting (h=−15000): d=0.2 µm. Pores < 0.2 µm hold unavailable water.
all_formulas.pitfall: Capillary equation assumes cylindrical pores. Real soil has irregular pores + connectivity.
all_formulas.decision: Macropore volume < 10% = compaction. Subsoil + add OM to restore structure.
all_formulas.notes: Macropores (>75 µm) conduct air + drain water. Mesopores (9-75 µm) hold available water. Micropores (<9 µm) hold unavailable water.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: حساب أحجام المسام من خصائص ماء التربة.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
d = قطر المسام
h = الجهد المصفوفي

all_formulas.name: Field Capacity Estimation (Saxton-Rawls)
all_formulas.variables:
%sand, %clay = texture
ρb = bulk density (g/cm³)
θ33 = water content at −33 kPa (field capacity)
all_formulas.purpose: Estimate field capacity from texture + bulk density without lab measurement. Used when only soil texture is known (e.g. from county soil survey).
all_formulas.example: Silt loam: 30% sand, 30% clay, ρb=1.35. θ33 ≈ 0.32 (32% by volume). TAW to wilting (θ1500≈0.18): 0.32−0.18 = 0.14 = 14% available.
all_formulas.pitfall: Accuracy ±3-5% water content. For irrigation design, confirm with actual lab test.
all_formulas.decision: Use Saxton-Rawls for planning + Rosetta for design. Replace estimates with measured values as data accumulates.
all_formulas.notes: Saxton + Rawls (1986). Other PTFs: Gupta-Larson, Bruand. Saxton-Rawls is most accessible (USDA-ARS online tool).
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تقدير السعة الحقلية من القوام والكثافة الظاهرية.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
%sand = الرمل
%clay = الطين
ρb = الكثافة الظاهرية

all_formulas.name: TDN from ADF (Acid Detergent Fiber)
all_formulas.variables:
ADF = acid detergent fiber (% DM)
TDN = total digestible nutrients (%)
all_formulas.purpose: Estimate TDN (energy) from ADF — a quick lab test. Higher ADF (more lignin) = lower digestibility = lower energy. Used for forage quality grading.
all_formulas.example: Alfalfa hay ADF=30%: TDN = 88.9 − 23.7 = 65.2%. Grass hay ADF=38%: TDN = 88.9 − 30 = 58.9%. Alfalfa has 10% more energy.
all_formulas.pitfall: Equation is for grasses + legumes. Corn silage uses different equation (NDF-based). Grain has ADF<5 but TDN>85.
all_formulas.decision: Beef cow mid-gestation needs 55% TDN. Lactation: 65%. Feed 60% TDN hay for maintenance, 65%+ for lactation.
all_formulas.notes: Rohweder et al. (1978). Modern labs use summative equation (NDF + CP + fat + ash) for higher accuracy.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تقدير الطاقة الكلية المهضومة من الألياف المنظمة بالحمض.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
ADF = الألياف المنظمة بالحمض
TDN = المغذيات الكلية المهضومة

all_formulas.name: Net Energy Maintenance (NEm) + Gain (NEg)
all_formulas.variables:
TDN% = total digestible nutrients
NEm = net energy for maintenance
NEg = net energy for gain (growth)
all_formulas.purpose: Convert TDN to net energy values used in NRC 2021 ration balancing. NEm keeps animal alive; NEg supports growth. Different feeds have different NEm:NEg ratios.
all_formulas.example: Corn silage TDN=70%: NEm = 70×0.0291−0.054 = 1.98 Mcal/kg. NEg = 70×0.0203−0.067 = 1.35 Mcal/kg. 400 kg steer needs 6.2 Mcal NEm/day → 3.1 kg corn silage DM for maintenance alone.
all_formulas.pitfall: NEm + NEg differ because growth is less efficient than maintenance. Don't use DE or ME for ration balancing — they overstate value.
all_formulas.decision: Compare feeds on $/Mcal NEg basis, not $/kg. Corn is usually cheapest energy source.
all_formulas.notes: NRC 2016 (beef). For dairy: NEL (net energy lactation) = TDN% × 0.0245 − 0.087.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تحويل TDN إلى قيم الطاقة الصافية المستخدمة في موازنة العليقة.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
TDN = المغذيات الكلية
NEm = طاقة الصيانة
NEg = طاقة النمو

all_formulas.name: Metabolizable Protein (MP)
all_formulas.variables:
MP = metabolizable protein (g/day)
RUP = rumen-undegradable protein (g)
MCP = microbial crude protein (g)
RDP = rumen-degradable protein (g)
0.13 = microbial yield (g MCP/g RDP TDN)
0.64 = MCP digestibility
all_formulas.purpose: Calculate MP — the protein actually absorbed in small intestine. Better than CP (crude protein) for ration balancing because it accounts for rumen fermentation.
all_formulas.example: Cow eats 1500 g CP, 65% degradable. RDP=975 g, RUP=525 g. MCP = 975 × 0.13 × 0.64 = 81 g. MP = 525 + 81 = 606 g/day. 600 kg lactating cow needs 1700 g MP — supplement with bypass protein.
all_formulas.pitfall: Microbial yield depends on energy (TDN) available in rumen. If energy-deficient, MCP drops even with high RDP.
all_formulas.decision: Balance RDP:RUP = 65:35 for high-producing dairy. For beef, 70:30 adequate.
all_formulas.notes: NRC 2001 (dairy) + 2016 (beef). Corn gluten meal + blood meal are high-RUP supplements.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: حساب البروتين الممتص فعلياً في الأمعاء الدقيقة.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
RUP = بروتين غير متحلل
MCP = بروتين ميكروبي
RDP = بروتين متحلل

all_formulas.name: Dry Matter Intake (Mertens Equation)
all_formulas.variables:
NDF = neutral detergent fiber (% DM)
BW = body weight (kg)
all_formulas.purpose: Predict dry matter intake from forage NDF. Higher NDF = more fill = less intake. Critical for ration formulation — intake drives production.
all_formulas.pitfall: Equation is for lactating dairy cows. Beef cows: DMI ≈ 2% BW. Feedlot: 2.5-3% BW.
all_formulas.decision: If DMI < predicted, check: forage quality (NDF >55% limits intake), mold/palatability, water availability, bunk space.
all_formulas.notes: Mertens (1987). Additive with fat: fat >5% of DM reduces DMI 2-5%.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: التنبؤ باستهلاك المادة الجافة من ألياف العلف.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
NDF = الألياف المنظمة المحايدة
BW = وزن الجسم

all_formulas.name: Milk Urea Nitrogen (MUN) Interpretation
all_formulas.variables:
MUN = milk urea nitrogen (mg/dL)
Normal range: 10–14 mg/dL
all_formulas.purpose: Interpret MUN as protein:energy balance diagnostic. High MUN = excess protein or deficient energy. Low MUN = protein deficiency. Saves $50-100/cow/year in feed cost.
all_formulas.example: Herd MUN = 18 mg/dL (high). Cause: overfeeding protein or underfeeding energy. Action: reduce CP by 1-2% or add 1 kg corn. Re-test in 2 weeks.
all_formulas.pitfall: MUN varies by breed (Jersey > Holstein), stage of lactation, season. Use herd average, not individual cow.
all_formulas.decision: MUN < 10: add protein. 10-14: balanced. >14: reduce protein or add energy. >18: significant waste + environmental N loss.
all_formulas.notes: DHIA labs report MUN with every test. Some inline milking systems measure MUN daily.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تفسير MUN كمؤشر لتوازن البروتين والطاقة.
all_formulas.variables_ar: MUN = نيتروجين يوريا الحليب

all_formulas.name: NDF Digestibility (NDFD)
all_formulas.variables:
NDF_initial = NDF before incubation
NDF_residual = NDF after 30 or 48 hr in vitro
all_formulas.purpose: Measure forage digestibility beyond TDN. High-NDFD forage (60%+) supports higher DMI + milk production. 1% NDFD increase = +0.4 L milk/day in dairy.
all_formulas.example: Corn silage NDF=40%, after 30 hr: 16% residual. NDFD = (40−16)/40 = 60%. Above 55% = excellent quality.
all_formulas.pitfall: NDFD varies by hybrid (BMR corn = +10%), maturity (late harvest = −10%), and storage (poor fermentation reduces NDFD).
all_formulas.decision: Pay $10-20/t premium for BMR corn silage — pays back via higher milk production.
all_formulas.notes: Commercial labs offer 30-hr (digestion rate) or 48-hr (potential digestibility) NDFD. 30-hr better predicts intake.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: قياس هضمية العلف بما يتجاوز TDN.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
NDF = الألياف المنظمة المحايدة
residual = المتبقي

all_formulas.name: Drinking Water Intake (Beef Cattle)
all_formulas.variables:
DMI = dry matter intake (kg/day)
BW = body weight (kg)
T = avg daily temp (°C)
ADG = average daily gain (kg)
all_formulas.purpose: Predict water intake for water system sizing + dehydration monitoring. Cattle drink 25-75 L/day depending on size + temp + production.
all_formulas.example: 400 kg feedlot steer, DMI=9 kg, ADG=1.5 kg, T=25°C: W = −5.34 + 4.41 + 72 + 20.75 + 0.06 = 91.9 L/day. Size waterer for 1.5× = 140 L.
all_formulas.pitfall: Water intake spikes 50-100% above 30°C (heat stress). Provide shade + extra water.
all_formulas.decision: Cattle drink 2-4× DMI in water. Provide 1 waterer per 20 head minimum, 2 per pen preferred.
all_formulas.notes: Winchester + Morris (1956). Lactating dairy cows drink 30% more than dry cows.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: التنبؤ باستهلاك الماء لتصميم نظام المياه ومراقبة الجفاف.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
DMI = استهلاك المادة الجافة
BW = الوزن
T = الحرارة
ADG = الزيادة اليومية

all_formulas.name: Rumen Degradable Protein (RDP) Balance
all_formulas.variables:
MCP_target = microbial protein needed (g/day)
0.13 = MCP yield per g RDP
0.64 = MCP digestibility
all_formulas.purpose: Balance rumen-degradable protein for microbial growth. Deficiency = microbes starve + reduced fiber digestion. Excess = wasted N + environmental loss.
all_formulas.example: Cow needs 1500 g MCP. RDP_req = 1500/0.13/0.64 = 18000 g... that's wrong. Let me recompute: MCP = RDP × 0.13 × 0.64. So RDP = MCP/(0.13×0.64) = 1500/0.0832 = 18,028 g RDP needed. If diet provides 20 kg RDP → surplus 2 kg (waste).
all_formulas.pitfall: RDP requirement depends on energy (TDN) available for microbial growth. Energy-deficient rumen can't use RDP efficiently.
all_formulas.decision: If RDP balance > +100 g: reduce urea or soybean meal. If < −100 g: add RDP source (urea cheapest).
all_formulas.notes: RDP sources: urea (100% degradable), soybean meal (70%), canola meal (65%). RUP sources: blood meal, corn gluten meal, fish meal.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: موازنة البروتين المتحلل لنمو الميكروبات في الكرش.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
MCP = البروتين الميكروبي
RDP = البروتين المتحلل

all_formulas.name: Herbicide Rate by Active Ingredient
all_formulas.variables:
AI_rate = required active ingredient (kg/ha or L/ha)
AI_concentration = % AI in product (e.g. 480 g/L = 48%)
all_formulas.purpose: Convert AI recommendation to product application rate. Labels often state 'apply 1.5 L product/ha' but AI rate is what matters for efficacy.
all_formulas.example: Glyphosate label: 1 kg AI/ha. Product 480 g/L (48%): Product = 1 × 100 / 48 = 2.08 L/ha.
all_formulas.pitfall: Read label units carefully: g/L vs % w/w vs % w/v. 480 g/L = 48% w/v (different from 48% w/w).
all_formulas.decision: Always calibrate sprayer to deliver target volume (L/ha). Product rate = AI rate × spray volume.
all_formulas.notes: AI rate depends on weed species + size + environmental conditions. Use label minimum to slow resistance.
all_formulas.name_ar: معدل مبيد الأعشاب حسب المادة الفعالة
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تحويل توصية المادة الفعالة إلى معدل تطبيق المنتج.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
AI = المادة الفعالة
concentration = التركيز

all_formulas.name: Tank Mix Order (WALES)
all_formulas.formula: Order: Wettable powders (WP) → Agitation → Liquids (L) → Emulsifiable concentrates (EC) → Solutions (S)
all_formulas.variables:
WP = wettable powder\WG = water-dispersible granule
SC = suspension concentrate
EC = emulsifiable concentrate
SL = soluble liquid
all_formulas.purpose: Correct tank-mix order prevents incompatibility (precipitation, gelling). Wrong order = spray tank full of sludge + lost product.
all_formulas.example: Mix glyphosate (SL) + atrazine (WG) + crop oil (EC). Order: 1) half-fill tank with water, 2) add atrazine WG (agitate), 3) add crop oil EC, 4) add glyphosate SL last, 5) top with water.
all_formulas.pitfall: Always do jar test first: mix small amounts in clear jar, shake, wait 30 min. If separation/precipitate → incompatible.
all_formulas.decision: Use compatibility agent (ammonium sulfate) if mixing glyphosate + hard water or many products.
all_formulas.notes: WALES acronym: Wettable, Agitate, Liquid, EC, Soluble. Some say 'A-PPLES': AG, powder, powder, liquid, EC, surfactant.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: ترتيب خلط الصحيح يمنع عدم التوافق (الترسب، التجلط).
all_formulas.variables_ar:
WP = مسحوق قابل للبلل
EC = مركز قابل للاستحلاب
SL = سائل قابل للذوبان

all_formulas.name: Rainfast Period (Hours Before Rain)
all_formulas.variables:
t_absorption = time for AI to enter leaf cuticle
Typical: glyphosate 4-6 hr, 2,4-D 1-2 hr, glufosinate 4 hr, dicamba 4-8 hr
all_formulas.purpose: Determine minimum rain-free window after spraying. Rain before rainfast = wasted application (washed off).
all_formulas.example: Spraying glyphosate at 6 AM, rain forecast at 11 AM (5 hr window). Glyphosate needs 6 hr rainfast. DON'T spray — wait for better window.
all_formulas.pitfall: Rainfast is shorter with adjuvants (crop oil, surfactant). Check label — some formulations are 'rainfast in 1 hr'.
all_formulas.decision: Use 24-hr rain-free forecast minimum. Use rainfast-enhancing adjuvant if window is short.
all_formulas.notes: Heavy dew can also wash off herbicide. Spray after dew dries (mid-morning) for best absorption.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تحديد الحد الأدنى للنافذة الخالية من المطر بعد الرش.
all_formulas.variables_ar: t_absorption = وقت الامتصاص

all_formulas.name: Herbicide Resistance Risk Score
all_formulas.variables:
n_applications = # times same MoA applied per year
years_consecutive = # consecutive years same MoA
weed_susceptibility = 1 (low) to 3 (high)
all_formulas.purpose: Score risk of selecting for herbicide-resistant weeds. Risk >6 = high probability of resistance within 5 years. Score >12 = resistance likely already present.
all_formulas.example: Glyphosate on ryegrass: 2 apps/year × 5 years × susceptibility 3 = risk 30. Very high — rotate MoA immediately.
all_formulas.pitfall: Resistance can develop in 3-5 years with same MoA. Once present, doesn't go away — manage forever.
all_formulas.decision: Rotate MoA (HRAC groups) every application. Mix 2+ MoAs per spray. Use non-chemical control (cultivation, cover crops).
all_formulas.notes: HRAC group codes: A (ACCase), B (ALS), C1 (PSII), G (EPSPS = glyphosate). Tank-mix different groups to delay resistance.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تقييم خطر تطور الأعشاب المقاومة لمبيدات الأعشاب.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
n = عدد التطبيقات
MoA = آلية العمل
years = السنوات المتتالية

all_formulas.name: Economic Injury Level (EIL) for Weeds
all_formulas.variables:
C = control cost ($/ha)
V = crop value ($/kg)
Y = weed-free yield (kg/ha)
P = proportional yield loss per weed (0–1)
b = regression coefficient
all_formulas.purpose: Calculate weed density at which control cost = yield loss benefit. Below EIL, don't spray (economic loss). Above EIL, spray.
all_formulas.example: Maize: C=$40/ha, V=$0.18/kg, Y=8000 kg/ha, P=0.02 per weed/m², b=0.95. EIL = 40/(0.18×8000×0.02×0.95) = 14.6 weeds/m². Below 15 weeds/m², don't spray.
all_formulas.pitfall: EIL assumes single weed species. Mixed weed flora needs separate EILs or combined model.
all_formulas.decision: Set action threshold (AT) below EIL (e.g. 60-70% of EIL) to allow time for control to work.
all_formulas.notes: Cousens (1985) rectangular hyperbola yield-loss model: YL = (I×d)/(1+(I×d/A)) where d=weed density.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: حساب كثافة الأعشاب التي تكون عندها تكلفة المكافحة تساوي خسارة الإنتاج.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
C = تكلفة المكافحة
V = قيمة المحصول
Y = الإنتاج
P = الخسارة لكل عشبة

all_formulas.name: Spray Volume by Weed Density + Canopy
all_formulas.variables:
V_base = base spray volume (L/ha, 80-150)
LAI = leaf area index (1–6)
weed_density = weeds/m²
all_formulas.purpose: Adjust spray volume for canopy density + weed pressure. Dense canopy + high weed pressure needs more volume for coverage.
all_formulas.pitfall: Higher volume = more drift (especially >200 L/ha with fine droplets). Use coarser droplets at high volume.
all_formulas.decision: Use 100-150 L/ha for systemic herbicides (glyphosate — translocated). 150-250 for contact (paraquat — needs coverage).
all_formulas.notes: Droplet size classification (ASABE S572): VF (very fine) drift-prone, F, M, C (coarse), VC. Use C-VC for systemic to reduce drift.
all_formulas.name_ar: حجم الرش حسب كثافة الأعشاب والغطاء
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تعديل حجم الرش لكثافة الغطاء وضغط الأعشاب.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
V_base = الحجم الأساسي
LAI = مؤشر مساحة الأوراق
weed_density = كثافة الأعشاب

all_formulas.name: Late Blight Forecast (Blitecast)
all_formulas.formula:
SV = max(0, (T − 7) × RH_factor) when RH ≥ 90% for ≥ 10 hr
Severity values accumulate; spray when SV ≥ 18
all_formulas.variables:
T = temperature during RH≥90% period (°C)
RH_factor = function of hours RH≥90%
SV = severity value (0–4 per day)
all_formulas.purpose: Predict potato/tomato late blight (Phytophthora infestans) risk. Accumulates severity values from weather data. First spray triggered at SV=18.
all_formulas.example: Day with 12 hr RH≥90% at 15°C: SV=4 (max). 5 days of similar weather: SV=20 → spray within 24 hr.
all_formulas.pitfall: Model calibrated for US Northeast. Local calibration needed for other climates. Use local leaf wetness sensor.
all_formulas.decision: If SV < 18: no spray. 18-30: first spray. >30: tighten spray interval to 5-7 days.
all_formulas.notes: Krause et al. (1975). Modern versions (e.g. SIMCAST) include fungicide wash-off by rain.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: التنبؤ بخطر لفحة البطاطس/الطماطم المتأخرة من بيانات الطقس.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
T = الحرارة
RH = الرطوبة النسبية
SV = قيمة الخطورة

all_formulas.name: Early Blight Forecast (TOMCAST)
all_formulas.formula:
DSV = f(leaf_wetness_hours × temperature)
Accumulate DSV; spray at DSV ≥ 15–35 (variety-dependent)
all_formulas.variables:
DSV = disease severity value (0–4 per day)
leaf_wetness = hours of leaf wetness
T = avg temp during wetness
all_formulas.purpose: Forecast tomato/potato early blight (Alternaria solani). Fewer sprays than calendar schedule — saves 2-4 applications per season.
all_formulas.example: Day with 14 hr leaf wetness at 18°C: DSV=3. Spray threshold 20: spray after 7 such days (vs. 14 calendar days).
all_formulas.pitfall: Leaf wetness sensor placement critical — place at canopy height, 30° angle, north-facing.
all_formulas.decision: Susceptible variety: spray at DSV 15. Resistant: DSV 25-35.
all_formulas.notes: Madden et al. (1978). Available as Decision Support System in most vegetable production areas.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: التنبؤ بلفحة الطماطم/البطاطس المبكرة.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
DSV = قيمة الخطورة
leaf_wetness = ساعات بلل الأوراق
T = الحرارة

all_formulas.name: Apple Scab (Mills Table)
all_formulas.formula:
Infection occurs when: leaf_wetness_hours ≥ f(T)
At 6°C: 18 hr wetness. At 16°C: 9 hr. At 20°C: 11 hr.
all_formulas.variables:
T = avg temperature during wetness (°C)
leaf_wetness_hours = consecutive hours of leaf wetness
all_formulas.purpose: Predict apple scab (Venturia inaequalis) infection periods. Primary infection occurs at green tip; secondary throughout season. Saves 2-4 fungicide sprays per season.
all_formulas.example: Apple at bloom, 10 hr leaf wetness at 14°C. Mills table: 12 hr needed at 14°C. No infection — no spray needed.
all_formulas.pitfall: Mills table is for primary infection (ascospores). Secondary (conidia) needs less wetness — 6 hr at 16°C.
all_formulas.decision: Apply protectant fungicide (captan) BEFORE infection period. After infection (within 24 hr): use eradicant (sterol inhibitor).
all_formulas.notes: Mills (1944). Modern versions adjust for relative humidity + ascospore maturity (ascospore dose model).
all_formulas.purpose_ar: التنبؤ بفترات إصابة جرب التفاح من بلل الأوراق والحرارة.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
T = الحرارة
leaf_wetness = ساعات بلل الأوراق

all_formulas.name: Fusarium Head Blight (FHB) Risk
all_formulas.formula:
Risk = f(T, RH, rainfall, crop_stage)
High risk when: T=15-30°C + RH>80% + rain>5mm during 7d pre-anthesis + 7d post-anthesis
all_formulas.variables:
T = temperature (°C)
RH = relative humidity (%)
rainfall = mm in past 7 days
crop_stage = anthesis (flowering) critical
all_formulas.purpose: Predict FHB (Fusarium graminearum) risk in wheat + barley. FHB produces DON mycotoxin — grain buyers reject >2 ppm DON. Saves crop from rejection.
all_formulas.example: Wheat at anthesis, T=22°C, RH=85%, rain=30mm past 7 days. High risk. Apply triazole fungicide (Prosaro/Caramba) within 5 days.
all_formulas.pitfall: Fungicide timing is critical: apply at early anthesis (Feekes 10.5.1), not before or after.
all_formulas.decision: If risk high: apply triazole within 5 days of anthesis start. If risk low: skip fungicide.
all_formulas.notes: FHB Risk Tool: http://www.wheatscab.psu.edu. Uses 7-day weather history + forecast.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: التنبؤ بخطر FHB في القمح من الطقس ومرحلة المحصول.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
T = الحرارة
RH = الرطوبة
rainfall = المطر
crop_stage = مرحلة المحصول

all_formulas.name: Downy Mildew (ONSET) Model
all_formulas.formula:
Sporulation when: 4°C ≤ T ≤ 25°C + RH≥90% ≥ 4 hr (night)
Infection when: leaf wetness ≥ 2 hr at 4–25°C
all_formulas.variables:
T = temperature (°C)
RH = relative humidity (%)
leaf_wetness = hours of leaf wetness
all_formulas.purpose: Forecast downy mildew (various oomycetes) on grapes, lettuce, cucurbits, onions. Night-time sporulation + morning infection cycle. Saves 3-5 fungicide sprays.
all_formulas.example: Grape vineyard, night T=18°C, RH=92% for 6 hr. Sporulation occurred. Morning: leaf wetness 4 hr at 20°C. Infection occurred. Apply fungicide within 24 hr.
all_formulas.pitfall: Downy mildew pathogens are oomycetes (water molds), not fungi. Use oomycete-specific fungicides (mefenoxam, phosphonates).
all_formulas.decision: Apply protectant before predicted infection period. Curative within 24 hr of infection.
all_formulas.notes: ONSET = Orangetip Need Spray Event Tracker. Various crop-specific models exist (PLASMOPARA for grape, Bremia for lettuce).
all_formulas.purpose_ar: التنبؤ بالبياض الزغبي على العنب والخس والقرعيات.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
T = الحرارة
RH = الرطوبة
leaf_wetness = بلل الأوراق

all_formulas.name: Infection Probability (Logistic Model)
all_formulas.variables:
T = temperature (°C)
W = wetness duration (hr)
a, b, c, d = pathogen-specific coefficients
all_formulas.purpose: General model for fungal infection probability. Used when specific forecast model unavailable. Coefficients available for 200+ pathogen-crop combinations.
all_formulas.example: Botrytis on strawberry: a=−5, b=0.2, c=0.15, d=0.005. At 20°C, 12 hr wetness: P = 1/(1+exp(−(−5+4+1.8+1.2))) = 1/(1+exp(−2)) = 0.88. 88% infection probability — spray.
all_formulas.pitfall: Logistic model assumes single wetness event. Multiple events need cumulative model.
all_formulas.decision: Spray when P > 0.5 (50% infection probability). Use protectant if P 0.3-0.5.
all_formulas.notes: Analytis (1977). Coefficients in EPPO + APS Crop Protection Compendium.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: نموذج عام لاحتمال الإصابة الفطرية.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
T = الحرارة
W = مدة البلل
a,b,c,d = معاملات

all_formulas.name: Leaching Requirement (Salinity)
all_formulas.variables:
EC_iw = electrical conductivity of irrigation water (dS/m)
EC_th = crop salinity threshold (dS/m)
all_formulas.purpose: Calculate extra water needed to leach salts below root zone. Without leaching, salts accumulate + eventually kill crops. Critical for arid-zone irrigation.
all_formulas.example: Tomato EC_th=2.5 dS/m, irrigation EC_iw=1.5: LR = 1.5/(5×2.5−1.5) = 0.13. Apply 13% extra water each irrigation to leach salts.
all_formulas.pitfall: LR is fraction of total water applied, not extra. If ET=100 mm + LR=0.15: total applied = 100/(1−0.15) = 117.6 mm.
all_formulas.decision: If LR > 0.3, water too salty for crop. Switch to tolerant crop (barley, date palm) or blend water.
all_formulas.notes: Rhoades (1974). FAO Irrigation + Drainage Paper 29 has crop salinity thresholds for 80+ crops.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: حساب المياه الإضافية اللازمة لغسل الأملاح تحت منطقة الجذور.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
EC_iw = موصلية ماء الري
EC_th = عتبة ملوحة المحصول

all_formulas.name: Adjusted SAR (Suarez)
all_formulas.variables:
SAR = Na / √((Ca+Mg)/2) in meq/L
pH = soil-water pH
Ca_change = change in Ca due to CO₂ + HCO₃
all_formulas.purpose: Adjust SAR for calcium precipitation tendency. Standard SAR overstates Na hazard when HCO₃ high — Ca precipitates as CaCO₃, leaving Na in solution. Adjusted SAR is more accurate.
all_formulas.example: Water SAR=8, HCO₃/Ca=2 (high). Standard SAR says OK (<10). Adjusted SAR might be 15 — actually high hazard. Use SAR_adj.
all_formulas.pitfall: Standard SAR (USDA 1954) is still used by most labs. Always check if reported SAR is adjusted or standard.
all_formulas.decision: SAR_adj < 3: safe. 3-9: marginal, add gypsum. >9: high hazard, avoid or treat.
all_formulas.notes: Suarez (1981). Modern version: SAR_adj = SAR × [1 + (8.4 − pH_c)], where pH_c is calculated from Ca + HCO₃ + CO₂.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تعديل SAR لميل الكالسيوم للترسيب.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
SAR = نسبة الصوديوم
pH = الحموضة
Ca = الكالسيوم

all_formulas.name: Langelier Saturation Index (LSI)
all_formulas.formula:
LSI = pH − pHs
pHs = (9.3 + A + B) − (C + D)
A = (TDS−1)/100; B = −13.12×log(T+273)+34.55; C = log(Ca²⁺); D = log(alkalinity)
all_formulas.variables:
pH = actual water pH
pHs = saturation pH
TDS, T, Ca²⁺, alkalinity = water chemistry
all_formulas.purpose: Predict CaCO₃ scaling tendency in pipes + drip emitters. LSI >0: scaling (clogs emitters). LSI <0: corrosive (eats pipes). LSI=0: balanced.
all_formulas.example: Drip irrigation water: pH=8.2, TDS=400, T=25°C, Ca=40 mg/L, alk=150 mg/L. pHs ≈ 7.4. LSI = 8.2−7.4 = +0.8. Scaling tendency — acidify.
all_formulas.pitfall: LSI is for CaCO₃ only. Iron + manganese scaling need separate calculations.
all_formulas.decision: LSI +0.5 to +1.0: add acid (sulfuric/nitric) to drop pH 0.5 units. >+1.0: install water treatment.
all_formulas.notes: Langelier (1936). For drip, target LSI = 0 to −0.5 (slightly corrosive, no scaling).
all_formulas.purpose_ar: التنبؤ بميل ترسيب CaCO₃ في الأنابيب والتنقيط.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
pH = الحموضة الفعلية
pHs = الحموضة عند التشبع

all_formulas.name: Nitrate Contamination Risk (DRASTIC)
all_formulas.formula: Risk = D × R × A × S × T × I × C × weight
all_formulas.variables:
D=depth to water, R=recharge, A=aquifer media, S=soil media, T=topography, I=impact vadose zone, C=conductivity
Each factor 1-10, weights sum to 100
all_formulas.purpose: Assess groundwater nitrate contamination risk from agricultural N. Helps decide N application rates + buffer zones near wells.
all_formulas.example: Shallow aquifer (D=2, weight 5) + sandy soil (S=9) + flat (T=10) + high recharge (R=8): Risk = 2×5×8×9×10×6×4×0.04 = 691. High risk — limit N to 100 kg/ha.
all_formulas.pitfall: DRASTIC is screening tool, not replacement for monitoring. Test well water annually for nitrate.
all_formulas.decision: Risk >150: implement N best management. >250: required NMP (nutrient management plan).
all_formulas.notes: EPA standard. Modified DRASTIC adds pesticide + nitrate leaching sub-models (DRASTIC-P, DRASTIC-N).
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تقييم خطر تلوث المياه الجوفية بالنترات من النيتروجين الزراعي.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
D = عمق الماء
R = التغذية
S = التربة
T = التضاريس

all_formulas.name: Drip Emitter Clogging Risk (Combined)
all_formulas.variables:
LSI_factor = 0 (LSI<0) to 10 (LSI>2)
TDS_factor = 0 (<500 mg/L) to 10 (>2000)
Fe_factor = 0 (<0.1 mg/L) to 10 (>1.0)
bio_factor = 0 (clean) to 10 (algae/bacteria)
all_formulas.purpose: Combined clogging risk for drip emitters. Single factor (e.g. LSI alone) misses multiple causes. Composite score identifies all contributors.
all_formulas.example: Water LSI=1.0 (score 5), TDS=1200 (score 6), Fe=0.5 (score 5), algae present (score 7). Risk = 0.4×5 + 0.3×6 + 0.2×5 + 0.1×7 = 2+1.8+1+0.7 = 5.5. Moderate — acidify + chlorinate.
all_formulas.pitfall: Bio-fouling is hardest to treat — requires chlorination + flushing, not just acid.
all_formulas.decision: Risk <3: low, flush monthly. 3-6: moderate, acidify + flush. >6: high, full treatment (filtration + acid + chlorine).
all_formulas.notes: Bucks + Nakayama (1980). Modern: add Mn + bacterial count factors. Use emitters with larger orifices (>1 mm) for high-risk water.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تقييم مركب لخطر انسداد نقاط الري بالتنقيط.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
LSI = مؤشر التشبع
TDS = إجمالي الأملاح الذائبة
Fe = الحديد
bio = بيولوجي

all_formulas.name: Soil Organic Carbon Stock
all_formulas.variables:
ρb = bulk density (g/cm³)
depth = sampling depth (cm)
%C = organic carbon %
all_formulas.purpose: Calculate SOC stock in t C/ha. Foundational measurement for carbon credit verification + tracking soil health trends.
all_formulas.pitfall: Bulk density changes with management (tillage reduces ρb). Always sample ρb + %C together, or stock changes are meaningless.
all_formulas.decision: Sample by genetic horizon (0-10, 10-20, 20-30 cm) for accurate stock. Composite 5+ cores per zone.
all_formulas.notes: Convert C to CO₂e: × 44/12 = × 3.667. 1% SOC in top 30 cm ≈ 148 t CO₂e/ha.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: حساب مخزون الكربون العضوي — أساس التحقق من ائتمانات الكربون.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
ρb = الكثافة الظاهرية
depth = العمق
%C = الكربون العضوي

all_formulas.name: SOC Stock Change (IPCC Tier 2)
all_formulas.formula: ΔSOC = (SOC_ref × F_LU × F_MG × F_I − SOC_ref) × t
all_formulas.variables:
SOC_ref = reference SOC stock
F_LU = land use factor
F_MG = management factor
F_I = input factor (organic amendments)
t = years
all_formulas.purpose: Estimate SOC change from management (tillage, cover crops, manure). Used by carbon credit protocols (Verra VM0042, Climate Action Reserve).
all_formulas.example: Conventional to no-till + cover crop: F_LU=1, F_MG=1.15 (no-till), F_I=1.11 (cover crop). ΔSOC = 50 × 1.15 × 1.11 − 50 = +6.3 t C/ha over 10 yr = 23 t CO₂e/ha.
all_formulas.pitfall: Tier 1 factors are generic. Tier 2 uses region-specific factors. Tier 3 uses measured data — most accurate.
all_formulas.decision: Carbon credits require 5-10 year commitment. Protocol verification costs $5,000-15,000. Minimum 1,000 acres to justify.
all_formulas.notes: IPCC 2006 Guidelines Ch 2. Default factors in Table 5.5. Verra VM0042 requires measured baseline + monitoring.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تقدير تغير الكربون العضوي من الإدارة الزراعية.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
SOC_ref = المخزون المرجعي
F_LU = عامل استخدام الأرض
F_MG = عامل الإدارة

all_formulas.name: N₂O Emission Factor (IPCC Tier 1)
all_formulas.variables:
N_applied = synthetic + organic N (kg/ha)
EF = emission factor (0.01 = 1% for synthetic)
44/28 = N₂O/N molecular weight ratio
all_formulas.purpose: Estimate direct N₂O emissions from N fertilizer. N₂O has 298× global warming potential of CO₂ — 1% of applied N becomes N₂O.
all_formulas.example: 200 kg N/ha urea: N₂O = 200 × 0.01 × 44/28 = 3.14 kg N₂O/ha = 936 kg CO₂e/ha. Significant — offset 30% with nitrification inhibitor.
all_formulas.pitfall: EF varies by climate (wet tropics: 1.6%) + fertilizer type (anhydrous ammonia higher). Tier 2 adjusts for these.
all_formulas.decision: Use nitrification inhibitors (DCD, DMPP) to reduce EF 30-50%. Split applications also reduce EF.
all_formulas.notes: IPCC 2006 Ch 11. Indirect N₂O (leaching + volatilization) adds 0.0075 kg N₂O/kg N leached.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: تقدير انبعاثات N₂O المباشرة من الأسمدة النيتروجينية.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
N_applied = النيتروجين المطبق
EF = عامل الانبعاث

all_formulas.name: Methane from Rice Paddies
all_formulas.variables:
EF = emission factor (kg CH₄/ha/day, 1.3 default)
t_flood = flood days
A = area (ha)
all_formulas.purpose: Calculate CH₄ emissions from flooded rice. Rice accounts for 12% of agricultural GHG. Mid-season drainage reduces 30-50%.
all_formulas.example: 1 ha rice, 100 flood days, EF=1.3: CH₄ = 1.3 × 100 × 1 = 130 kg CH₄/ha = 3,640 kg CO₂e/ha.
all_formulas.pitfall: EF varies by water regime: continuous flood 1.3, intermittent 0.5, single drainage 0.9.
all_formulas.decision: Alternate Wetting + Drying (AWD) reduces 30-70% CH₄ with no yield loss. Practice eligible for carbon credits.
all_formulas.notes: IPCC 2006 Ch 4. AWD: drain when water drops 15 cm below soil, reflood. Saves water too.
all_formulas.purpose_ar: حساب انبعاثات الميثان من الأرز المغمور.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
EF = عامل الانبعاث
t_flood = أيام الغمر
A = المساحة

all_formulas.name: Carbon Credit Eligibility
all_formulas.formula: Eligible if: Additionality + Permanence (≥25 yr) + Measurement + No double-counting + Co-benefits
all_formulas.variables:
Additionality = practice wouldn't happen without credit payment
Permanence = reversal buffer (10-20%)
Measurement = baseline + monitoring (5-10 yr)
Co-benefits = biodiversity, water, social
all_formulas.purpose: Screen farm for carbon credit eligibility. Even if math checks out, protocols require these 5 criteria. Saves months of wasted protocol review.
all_formulas.example: Farm adopts cover crops in 2025. Eligible if: (1) didn't do before (additionality), (2) commit through 2050 (permanence), (3) sample soil 2025 + 2030 (measurement), (4) not in other program (double-counting), (5) document pollinator habitat (co-benefits).
all_formulas.pitfall: Additionality is hardest — if cover crops already common in area, may not qualify. 'Practice-based' vs. 'outcome-based' protocols differ.
all_formulas.decision: Talk to aggregator (Indigo, Nori, Truterra) before starting. They handle protocol + buyer matching.
all_formulas.notes: Voluntary markets: Verra (VCS), Gold Standard, CAR. Compliance: CA Cap-and-Trade, RGGI. Prices: $5-30/t CO₂e (voluntary), $15-50 (compliance).
all_formulas.purpose_ar: فحص المزرعة لأهلية ائتمانات الكربون.
all_formulas.variables_ar:
Additionality = الإضافة
Permanence = الديمومة
Measurement = القياس

all_formulas.name: Fuel-Based CO₂ (Diesel)
all_formulas.variables:
L_diesel = liters of diesel
2.68 = kg CO₂ per L diesel
all_formulas.purpose: Calculate farm fuel carbon footprint. Tractor operations are 20-40% of farm emissions. Used for carbon footprint labels + reduction planning.
all_formulas.example: Tractor uses 50 L/ha for tillage + planting + spraying: CO₂ = 50 × 2.68 = 134 kg CO₂/ha. 100 ha farm = 13.4 t CO₂.
all_formulas.pitfall: 2.68 is for diesel. Gasoline: 2.31. LPG: 1.51. Propane: 1.51. Biodiesel: 1.2 (biogenic, lower).
